author: D. D. Manning
title: Westport Rehabilitation and Nursing Center ownership and CMS rating detailed for Q1 2026
text:
In the first quarter of 2026, Virginia Care Holco, LLC owned Westport Rehabilitation and Nursing Center, based on Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) records . Located in Henrico County, the facility has operated under Virginia Care Holco, LLC since Jan. 1, 2020.
The nursing home operates as a for-profit business.
During this time frame, Westport Rehabilitation and Nursing Center received an overall CMS rating of one. This score is below Virginia’s state nursing home average of 3.0. CMS assesses nursing homes using metrics that include health inspection results, staffing, and the quality of care given to residents.
Data show Westport Rehabilitation and Nursing Center served an average of 189.1 residents daily in the first quarter of 2026, with a total capacity of 225 beds. The facility does not have a hospital-based status.
During the first quarter, Westport Rehabilitation and Nursing Center incurred two fines totaling $62,848 and faced two separate penalties.
Henrico County, Virginia, had a total of 11 for-profit nursing facilities during the same period.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the country’s older adult population keeps expanding while younger age groups are shrinking. From 2020 to 2024, Americans age 65 and over grew by 13%, but the number under 18 decreased by 1.7%. Over the last 100 years, the older adult population in the U.S. surged from 4.9 million in 1920 to more than 61 million in 2024.
A 2021 study found that almost half of adults in this demographic—about 28 million—could need long-term services and support. The report also predicts more than a third may ultimately require nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
